### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. lissencephaly due to TUBA1A mutation  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.486)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-190840, Reactome:R-HSA-3371497, Reactome:R-HSA-380320, Reactome:R-HSA-389977, Reactome:R-HSA-5610787)

**Proposed mechanism:** TUBA1A (HGNC:11576) —DISRUPTS→ alpha-tubulin folding and stability (GO:0008137); TUBB2B (HGNC:12122) —DISRUPTS→ beta-tubulin folding and stability (GO:0008137); alpha-tubulin folding and stability (GO:0008137) —LEADS_TO→ microtubule cytoskeleton organization (GO:0007010); beta-tubulin folding and stability (GO:0008137) —LEADS_TO→ microtubule cytoskeleton organization (GO:0007010); microtubule cytoskeleton organization (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ neuronal migration (GO:0001708); neuronal migration (GO:0001708) —LEADS_TO→ Cortical dysplasia (HP:0002099); neuronal migration (GO:0001708) —LEADS_TO→ Lissencephaly (HP:0001309). Mutations in TUBA1A (Disease B) and TUBB2B (Disease A) disrupt the folding and stability of alpha- and beta-tubulin subunits, respectively. This impairment leads to defects in overall microtubule cytoskeleton organization, which in turn disrupts proper neuronal migration, ultimately resulting in the distinct but overlapping phenotypes of cortical dysplasia and lissencephaly.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of a pathogenic variant in TUBA1A or TUBB2B that exhibits a gain-of-function mechanism or does not impact microtubule organization or neuronal migration would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: A pathogenic variant in TUBA1A or TUBB2B with a frequency > 0.01% in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of microtubule dynamics in these distinct neuronal migration disorders could reveal common therapeutic targets for enhancing neuronal development and potentially mitigating the severity of these conditions.
